facts.statement: The type species was originally named in 1958 but was redescribed as Maomingosuchus in 2017.
facts.quote: The type species, originally Tomistoma petrolica, was named in 1958 and was redescribed as Maomingosuchus in 2017.

facts.statement: A second species was described in 2022 from deposits in northern Vietnam that are dated to 39–35 million years ago.
facts.quote: A second species, Maomingosuchus acutirostris, was described in 2022 from middle-upper Eocence deposits (late Bartonian–Priabonian age, 39–35 Ma) of the Na Duong Basin in northern Vietnam.

facts.statement: This animal lived during the Late Eocene in Southeast Asia.
facts.quote: Maomingosuchus is an extinct genus of gavialoid crocodylian from Late Eocene of Southeast Asia.

facts.statement: Fossils have been found in Priabonian-aged deposits in China and possibly Thailand.
facts.quote: It was discovered in Priabonian-aged deposits of China and possibly also Thailand.

facts.statement: It was a relatively small crocodile with an estimated length of 3 to 3.5 meters.
facts.quote: It was a relatively small gavialoid with an estimated total length of 3 - 3.5 m.

facts.statement: Scientists propose it is either a basal member of Gavialoidea or belongs to the family Tomistominae.
facts.quote: It is proposed to be a basal member of Gavialoidea, or alternatively within the family Tomistominae.

facts.statement: Its parent group is classified as Tomistominae.
It belongs to the family Gavialidae.
The animal lived between 48.07 and 33.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Lutetian to Priabonian (48.07 to 33.9 million years ago)
